_note: Money is Thuso Money: payments, payouts, wallets, vouchers, gifts, group wallets, claims and Market orders. Every write is idempotent with a key. MyThuso never holds a card number. Wave 2 contract; Waves 3 and 5 build.

doorsToAdd.why: The switching partner's claim responses are supplier callbacks; a door to add.

refusals.statement: MyThuso never holds a card number.
refusals.why: The provider's page takes it.

refusals.statement: A payout line does not name its own amount for a visit.
refusals.why: The share is packages/catalog/earnings.json's arithmetic.

refusals.statement: A suspension never touches money already earned.
refusals.why: Money does not subscribe to a suspension.

refusals.statement: A scheme receives nothing about a person's grant.
refusals.why: Money serves only the scheme's aggregate role.

refusals.statement: Nothing is charged without an idempotency key.
refusals.why: A retry is not a second charge. The binder asks for the key before either payment route's handler runs, and the ledger asks again, so both routes are named in case it is ever reached.

refusals.statement: Money does not hear that event.
refusals.why: Money hears the billable state changes packages/catalog/events.json lists under moneyHears, and an event carrying a reference into the record is refused even when its type is on the list.

refusals.statement: No doctor's payout is scheduled while the fee is undecided.
refusals.why: The documents give a range for a doctor's per-case fee, not a price. packages/catalog/money.json holds the fee as null until somebody named decides it, and a payout worked out from a number nobody decided is a promise nobody made.

refusals.statement: No scheme or employer sees what one person paid.
refusals.why: A scheme and an employer are served in aggregate. A person's payment tells whoever reads it that a visit happened, and when.

refusals.statement: That door is locked until its switch-on conditions are evidenced.
refusals.why: Payment results and payout advice arrive only through the doors in packages/catalog/feeds.json, and none of their conditions is met. In development the simulated provider stands behind them, in process, and nothing from the network does.

refusals.statement: This cash payment has had too many wrong codes and is held for the operations desk.
refusals.why: packages/catalog/money.json's attemptLimit. A six-digit code that can be tried without limit is a code that can be walked; after the limit even the right code is refused until the desk releases the payment.

refusals.statement: Cash is recorded against a finished visit, and this one has not finished.
refusals.why: A cash code entered before Care says the visit was billable would record money for a visit that may still not happen.

refusals.statement: This visit has no price Money can read yet, so nothing is charged.
refusals.why: appointment.booked@2 names the service, so the payable it opens is priced from packages/catalog/services.json as it opens. A payable can still have no price: one a store opened under appointment.booked@1, which named no service and is withdrawn, stays unpriced until visit.billable@1 names one. A charge against a payable with no catalogue price is an amount that came from the caller.

refusals.statement: A payout does not go down without a line naming the visit and the reason.
refusals.why: packages/catalog/earnings.json's every-deduction-is-named rule, enforced on the ledger rather than only drawn on the screen.

keptOnRefusal.why: A wrong code is refused, and the refusal rolls back everything else the handler did. The count of wrong codes and the audit row saying who entered one and when must survive that refusal, or the attempt limit never bites and a code can be walked by trying.

withdrawn.why: Built on the runtime, it had no true answer for two things a nurse can send. A reference to no cash payment could only be refused as a wrong code, which would count an attempt against nothing, or as a visit not finished, which is false. A nurse who does not hold the visit could only be told her role may not call the route, and a nurse's role may. Version two adds payable-not-found and cash-code-not-your-visit and keeps everything else. Its callers are version two's.

refusals.why: The nurse visit.billable@1 names is the one the patient paid at the door. Another nurse is refused before a code is compared, so she can neither record the cash nor use up the attempts of the nurse who was there.

keptOnRefusal.why: A wrong code is refused, and the refusal rolls back everything else the handler did. The count of wrong codes and the audit row saying who entered one and when must survive that refusal, or the attempt limit never bites and a code can be walked by trying.

secretRequestFields.why: The patient's cash code. The runtime keeps a digest of every accepted request's fields to refuse a reused key; a digest of six digits would be the six digits to anybody holding the store file, so the code is left out of it.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same act once.

response.why: The payment's state, unchanged: releasing a hold pays nothing.

refusals.statement: Nothing is owed under that reference.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: A release lets the nurse try again; the payment is published when the right code is entered.

withdrawn.why: It released a hold with no reason and had no field to carry one, so the audit of a release could say who and when and never why — and a hold lifted for no recorded reason is a code that can be walked five attempts at a time. Nor could it refuse releasing a payment that was not held. Version two takes a reason code from packages/catalog/money.json and refuses a release without one, with one the desk is not given, and of a payment that is not held. Its callers are version two's.

routes.summary: The operations desk releases a cash payment held for too many wrong codes, after speaking to the patient, with the reason written down.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same release once, and the audit gains one row.
The held cash payment, Money's own.

Why the hold is released, as one of packages/catalog/money.json's cash.releaseReasons: a code rather than free text, because the audit is read by finance and a desk's own words about a patient are where health information goes. Asked for by the handler rather than the binder, so that a release without one is refused in its own sentence.

response.why: The payment's state, unchanged: releasing a hold pays nothing.

refusals.statement: Nothing is owed under that reference.
refusals.why: Only a cash payment with a code can be held or released.

refusals.statement: A held cash payment is released with a reason, or it is not released.
refusals.why: A hold is what stops a six-digit code being walked. Lifting it for no recorded reason gives whoever is trying another five attempts, and nobody reading the audit afterwards can tell a desk that spoke to the patient from one that pressed a button.

refusals.statement: That is not one of the reasons a held cash payment is released for.
refusals.why: The reasons are packages/catalog/money.json's. A reason nobody declared is a word nothing reads, and the audit is only useful if every row means something somebody agreed.

refusals.statement: This cash payment is not held, so there is nothing to release.
refusals.why: A release resets the wrong-code count. On a payment that is not held that would be a quiet way to hand a nurse, or whoever holds her phone, a fresh set of attempts.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: A release lets the nurse try again; the payment is published when the right code is entered. No engine acts on a hold being lifted, and the event contract refuses an event nobody reads.

Each setting: its key, type, unit, the value in force and the version that set it, its default and provenance, its limits, who may change it, what a change reaches, its guardrail, and its clinical review.

routes.summary: Change one Money setting, with a reason, against the version in force. A changed fee reaches cases signed after it and never one already signed, and a plan's wording reaches plan screens opened after it.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same change once, and the history gains one row.
The setting's key, from the settings block of the engine's own contract.
The new value, for a setting in minutes, a count, cents or a percentage.
The new value, for a setting that is on or off.
The new value, for a setting that is one of a few named choices.
The new wording, for a setting patients or nurses read.
The new roles, for a setting that names roles from packages/catalog/vetting.json.
The new rota, for a setting that is windows of a post, days and hours. A post, never a named person.
The new values, for a setting that is a list.
The new values, for a setting whose parts change together.
Why. Asked for by the handler rather than the binder, so that a change without one is refused in its own sentence rather than the general one for a missing field.
The settings version the admin was looking at. A change against an older one is refused.

response.why: When it took effect. Whatever started before it keeps the version it started under.

refusals.statement: Only the role a setting names changes it, and the change is recorded against a named person.
refusals.why: A setting decides how the platform treats people. The role or capability the setting names changes it, and a change is recorded against somebody who can be asked about it; everybody else only reads what is in force.

refusals.statement: There is no setting by that name.
refusals.why: An unknown setting is refused rather than stored, or the history fills with changes nothing reads.

refusals.statement: A change to a setting says why, or it is not made.
refusals.why: The history is read after something has gone wrong. A change with no reason is a number somebody moved.

refusals.statement: These settings changed after you opened them. Read what is in force now and decide against that.
refusals.why: Two admins changing one setting from screens opened at the same time would each overwrite a decision they never saw.

refusals.statement: That is not the kind of value this setting holds.
refusals.why: A word where a number belongs, or a list where one choice belongs, is a guess at what the admin meant, and a setting is never set by a guess.

refusals.statement: This setting is never nought or less, whatever its range says.
refusals.why: A wait of nothing, an offer that lapses as it is made and a fee of nothing are never what anybody meant. The range is a proposal and could be set wrongly; this refusal does not depend on it.

refusals.statement: Every role a setting names is a role on the vetting register.
refusals.why: A role the register does not hold is a gate nobody can be vetted through, which looks like a shortage rather than a mistake.

refusals.statement: That wording is longer than this setting allows.
refusals.why: The maximum is the space the words are read in. Wording that does not fit is cut off where somebody reads it.

refusals.statement: That wording drops a sentence this setting must always keep.
refusals.why: Some wording carries a promise that protects somebody. It may be reworded around that sentence and never without it.

refusals.statement: That rota leaves hours uncovered that must always have somebody on them.
refusals.why: A rota with a gap is an alert with nobody to go to, and nobody finds out until one arrives.

refusals.statement: That is outside what an admin may set for this setting.
refusals.why: The bounds, the allowed values and the allowed roles sit beside the default in the engine's contract. Moving a setting past them is a change to that contract, not a setting.

refusals.statement: That is already the value in force, so there is nothing to change.
refusals.why: A change that changes nothing is a row in the history saying something happened when nothing did.

refusals.statement: A nurse's share is never worded as a fraction or a percentage. It is shown to the rand on each visit, because it is not the same part of every visit.
refusals.why: packages/catalog/services.json pays a nurse three quarters of most visits and less of a screening bundle and of Thuso SOS. Asked by packages/engines/src/money/domain/settings.ts from packages/catalog/money.json's wordingRules, after the shared rules.

refusals.statement: A plan's name never sounds like medical aid, a scheme, cover or insurance.
refusals.why: packages/catalog/mom-plans.json refuses a plan being read as medical aid, and a name is read before any sentence. Asked from packages/catalog/money.json's wordingRules, after the shared rules.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: No engine acts on a settings change. The engine that owns a setting reads the value in force when it starts something, and the event contract refuses an event nobody subscribes to. A change is the row it appends to the engine's own history, which the read route returns.
